title: Breton Kingdoms
capsule: The Breton kingdoms were a cluster of early medieval polities in the Armorican peninsula (modern Brittany), including Domnonée in the north, Cornouaille in the southwest, and Bro Waroc'h (later Vannes) in the southeast, which emerged following the migration of Brittonic Celts from southwestern Britain in the fifth and sixth centuries. The kingdoms operated under their own law codes (Lex Britannica), maintained close ecclesiastical and cultural ties with Wales and Cornwall, and successfully resisted Frankish domination through most of the seventh and eighth centuries under rulers such as Waroch II. Carolingian pressure intensified under Charlemagne and Louis the Pious; Nominoë, recognized as count by Louis the Pious in 831, united the Breton polities and defeated Charles the Bald at the Battle of Ballon (845), effectively establishing Breton independence as the Duchy of Brittany.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The internal boundaries among the Breton kingdoms are poorly attested; they are reconstructed largely from hagiographic texts and ecclesiastical records rather than administrative documents, and the extent of each sub-kingdom is approximate.
